title: Do not dispatch a reviewer onto a PR that is not mergeable; hold review_ready with a wait reason until the owner rebases

owned: the matching veto in task_execution_dispatch_candidate (.orchestrator/supervisor.py) and evaluate_task_delivery_admission (.orchestrator/dispatch_policy.py)
the in-memory review-dispatch hold diagnostic registry in .orchestrator/supervisor.py
RESPONSIBILITY_TRANSFER_EVENT_TYPES and canonical_worker_terminal_status recognizing a governed blocker as a valid end-of-responsibility event (.orchestrator/supervisor.py)
not_changing: PLAN-002 (the underlying shared-file bff_test_architecture_inventory.json contention that produces DIRTY PRs in the first place) -- explicitly out of scope per the task brief

live GitHub polling of a PR's mergeStateStatus -- no prober exists yet to populate delivery_binding.pr_merge_state; this change is fail-open on absent data and does not add that poller (see failure_reproduction below)

.orchestrator/worker_runner.py -- it only tracks child-process exit_code/runner_status and has no awareness of which ai-status.sh subcommand ran; the terminal-status classification already lived entirely in supervisor.py's activity-log-driven canonical_worker_terminal_status, so no worker_runner.py change was needed
the existing review/approve/reopen DIRTY-PR rejection in scripts/git/github_review_bridge.py -- unchanged; this task only stops the wasted dispatch that happens before that rejection is ever reached
composes_with: any future async prober that writes delivery_binding.pr_merge_state (e.g. extending probe_demanded_delivery_health or a new dedicated PR-health probe) -- the hold activates automatically once such a prober exists, no further planner change required
the reviewer's own governed `ai-status.sh blocker` call, which is the mechanism that durably records the wait reason on the canonical task row once a running reviewer discovers a DIRTY PR mid-review

failure_reproduction.case: 2026-09-17: tasks CB02/CB05/CB07 sat in `review` with their PR DIRTY against dev (shared-file conflict in bff_test_architecture_inventory.json, tracked separately as PLAN-002). The planner kept emitting review_ready_dispatch for them anyway.
failure_reproduction.prior_outcome: The dispatched reviewer completed a full review, then canonical `approve`/`reopen` rejected it because the PR was DIRTY. The reviewer worker exited, but its exit event type (blocker, if it filed one) was not in RESPONSIBILITY_TRANSFER_EVENT_TYPES, so canonical_worker_terminal_status returned None and the supervisor's poll loop treated the exit as worker_process_missing and redispatched. 18:50Z-22:50Z: 345 worker_lost_lease events, per-task generation churn, three provider accounts exhausted, plus 20 post_dispatch_maintenance re-verification conflicts.
failure_reproduction.regression: test_dirty_pr_merge_state_holds_review_dispatch_admission and test_mergeable_or_unknown_pr_merge_state_still_dispatches_reviewer in .orchestrator/test_supervisor.py exercise both the supervisor.py diagnostics ladder (task_execution_dispatch_candidate) and the live planning ladder (dispatch_policy.py's evaluate_task_delivery_admission) for DIRTY/CONFLICTING/BLOCKED_CONFLICT vs. MERGEABLE/UNKNOWN/absent merge states. test_canonical_worker_terminal_status_recognizes_reviewer_blocker, test_canonical_worker_terminal_status_recognizes_owner_blocker, and test_missing_process_without_blocker_is_still_lost_lease prove a governed blocker-then-exit is now recognized as a clean responsibility transfer for both roles, while an unrelated dead process with no transfer event is still correctly treated as worker_process_missing.

implementation.admission_hold: review_dispatch_pr_conflict_hold_reason(task) in .orchestrator/rewrite/task_machine.py reads task['delivery_binding']['pr_merge_state'] (uppercased); if it is DIRTY, CONFLICTING, or the conflict-specific BLOCKED_CONFLICT (deliberately distinct from GitHub's ambiguous bare BLOCKED, which also covers unmet branch-protection requirements a reviewer can still act on), it returns a reason string, else None. task_execution_dispatch_candidate (supervisor.py) and evaluate_task_delivery_admission (dispatch_policy.py) both veto a REVIEW_READY decision when this fires, matching the existing delivery_binding_is_current / is_non_default_repository_finalization_pending veto pattern already used in both ladders. dispatch_policy.py's evaluate_task_delivery_admission is the ladder the live per-cycle planner (dispatch_ready_tasks) actually calls; supervisor.py's task_execution_dispatch_candidate is used for diagnostics, stale-event revalidation, and recovery-replacement reservation -- both had to receive the veto.
implementation.fail_open_by_design: No prober currently populates delivery_binding.pr_merge_state (none existed in the codebase to reuse -- the delivery_health mechanism tracks provider/account health, not PR merge state, and scripts/git/auto_integrator.py's DIRTY handling is a separate CLI script at merge time, not a per-task cached fact reachable from the IO-free planner). The hold therefore fails open on missing/unrecognized values, preserving today's dispatch behavior until a future prober writes this field; wiring that live poller is left as a follow-up, out of scope for this task.
implementation.diagnostic_registry: record_review_dispatch_hold_diagnostic / review_dispatch_hold_diagnostic / clear_review_dispatch_hold_diagnostic in .orchestrator/supervisor.py give an inspectable in-memory record of a skipped dispatch (task_execution_dispatch_candidate is a pure, IO-free query called every planning tick and from several non-planning call sites, so it must not write the canonical status file itself). The durable canonical blocked/waiting_for row for the same DIRTY-PR condition is filed out-of-band by the reviewer's own governed `ai-status.sh blocker` call.
implementation.blocker_recognized_as_terminal: RESPONSIBILITY_TRANSFER_EVENT_TYPES now includes "blocker" (already a member of GOVERNANCE_LIFECYCLE_EVENT_TYPES). canonical_worker_terminal_status's valid_statuses map gains "blocker": frozenset({"blocked"}). No additional role restriction was added -- the function's existing exact-actor-match check already fails closed on a mismatched owner/reviewer, and a blocker may legitimately be filed by either role, so this generalizes the fix beyond just the reviewer/DIRTY-PR case to any worker that files a governed blocker before exiting.
implementation.worker_runner_unchanged: worker_runner.py has no notion of which ai-status.sh subcommand ran; the terminal-status classification lives entirely in supervisor.py, so no change was required there.

pre_existing_base_failure_proof.detail: Fails identically on an unmodified checkout of this same branch base (confirmed by stashing all task changes via `git stash push -u`, re-running in isolation, then restoring by exact stash SHA). It asserts scripts/ai_status.py does not contain certain forbidden reassignment-event-id string fragments (e.g. "supervisor-reassign-") that are unrelated to this task's dispatch_policy/supervisor/task_machine changes -- a pre-existing repository condition, not a regression introduced here.
pre_existing_base_failure_proof.result_after_restoring_task_changes: test_supervisor.py alone re-verified clean: 360 passed, 81 subtests passed
